text:
It took me many decades to figure out what probably everyone else already knows: real private pathology exists. But pathology is also like mold: it festers when the environment is perfect for it.

The dominant culture creates that environment.

It does that by turning the couple into a private little world. One person is expected to become lover, family, community, therapist, and future. Then whatever damage happens between them gets treated as a private failure.

We help make the romantic myths real too. We treat jealousy as proof of love, promise feelings nobody can promise, hide the conflict, and if it ends, treat the ending itself as proof that the relationship failed.

Then we suffer inside ideas that were never natural laws, and we walk blindly into our first, second, third, fourth, and fifth marriages!

Speaking of which, I wish I’d prioritized understanding the basic fears, desires, traumas, values, strengths, and weaknesses of the women I got close to in a more conscious manner. Instead, I often went with the flow of conversation and hanging out until closeness had built itself before we had decided what it meant.
